+## #3815 - One external agent drives SolidCraft and CamCraft
+
+**Decided:** Add one guide under `docs/user-guide/` and link it from the
+README. Use Claude Code's project configuration as the concrete client
+example. Give both CLI bridge arguments and separate ports. Use a one-body
+millimetre plate with one through hole, followed by a CamCraft drill
+operation on pre-sized stock. Document STEP as the fallback when the native
+cache is incompatible.
+
+**Why:** This documents the external-agent path that exists now. The live
+CamCraft registry, source restrictions and public SolidCraft documentation
+supply the contracts. Separate server labels prevent ambiguous calls such
+as `undo`. Explicit verification, file-link and approval steps avoid an
+implied automatic CAD-to-NC pipeline.
+
+**Considered and dropped:** Do not implement the proposed in-app MCP client
+or its privacy policy from research #3793. Those are separate issues. Do
+not add client-specific examples for every agent, duplicate the full tool
+reference, install SolidCraft, or run a broad app build for prose. A
+source/help check is not a two-app runtime acceptance result. State that
+limit in the guide and PR. Do not imply in-app cloud controls govern an
+external client. No process files or runtime code change.
+
+**Cost to change later:** Update one guide when a CLI, MCP schema or native
+cache contract changes. A future tested two-app example can replace the
+source-checked walkthrough without changing application code. The
+repository's review-time light lane is not run for this prose-only slice;
+focused link and schema checks are the verification for this task.

+# Drive SolidCraft and CamCraft with one external agent
+
+One external MCP client, such as Claude Code, can connect to both desktop
+apps in one conversation. SolidCraft makes the part. CamCraft imports the
+saved geometry and programs its cuts. This is not CamCraft's built-in AI
+Chat acting as a SolidCraft client.
+
+This guide uses local files and two visible desktop windows. It stops at
+software verification. It does not run a machine or establish machine safety.
+The command examples were checked against source and help, not exercised as
+a complete two-app session. Use the tool schemas of your installed versions.
+
+## Connect both windows
+
+Install both desktop apps and their matching CLIs first. Put the CLIs on
+`PATH`, or use their full executable paths below. Create a dedicated local
+folder for this example. The folder must exist before SolidCraft starts.
+Replace `/home/USER/cad-cam-demo` with its absolute path everywhere below.
+Do not give an agent access to your whole home folder.
+
+Start the apps in separate terminals:
+
+```sh
+solidcraft --control 7878
+camcraft-ui --mcp-port 7879
+```
+
+These are two different loopback ports, not HTTP URLs. Keep them local;
+do not forward them to another computer or expose them publicly. SolidCraft
+reads the control token from the file its app writes for that port. Do not
+copy the token into a chat or client configuration. See its public
+[MCP documentation](https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft/blob/69ac4646de58dc64befd804157e95120a1622803/docs/mcp.md)
+for sandboxed packages and token-file discovery.
+
+For Claude Code, merge these entries into the project's `.mcp.json`.
+Preserve any existing entries. Replace executable names with full paths if
+needed. On Windows, escape backslashes in JSON paths as `\\`.
+
+```json
+{
+  "mcpServers": {
+    "solidcraft": {
+      "command": "solidcraft-cli",
+      "args": ["mcp", "--connect", "127.0.0.1:7878", "--allow-path", "/home/USER/cad-cam-demo"]
+    },
+    "camcraft": {
+      "command": "camcraft-cli",
+      "args": ["mcp", "--connect", "127.0.0.1:7879"]
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Restart the client and approve the two server entries. Each client-facing
+server speaks MCP over stdio. Each CLI bridges to its own app window.
+For another MCP client, use its stdio-server configuration format with the
+same commands and argument arrays; `.mcp.json` is specific to Claude Code.
+Do not register these ports as Streamable HTTP endpoints.
+
+Use the client's tool listing to confirm both connections. Ask SolidCraft
+for `version {}` and `inspect_design {}`. Ask CamCraft for `get_job {}`.
+Confirm that the replies describe the intended windows before making changes.
+The client can prefix tool names with a server name. In this guide,
+**SolidCraft** and **CamCraft** identify the server; the names in code are
+the tools each server publishes, before client-specific prefixes.
+
+Without `--connect`, CamCraft creates a separate headless document. Its
+window will not show those edits. Its headless server records model links
+but does not run the window's file watcher.
+
+## Example: a plate with one through hole
+
+Use empty example documents, not an existing job. Save any existing work
+before you start. Tell the agent:
+
+> Use SolidCraft to make one millimetre plate, 40 by 30 by 10, with one
+> 6 mm through hole at X20 Y15. Save it locally. Import it into CamCraft
+> and prepare one drill operation on a pre-sized blank. Generate and
+> verify, but do not post. Ask before machine or post changes. Stop on
+> every error or unexpected dimension. Do not send screenshots or CAD
+> data to a cloud provider without my explicit permission.
+
+### 1. Make and save the part in SolidCraft
+
+Check that SolidCraft's document units are millimetres. Use its
+`describe_command` tool with `{"id":"solid.box"}` and
+`{"id":"solid.hole"}` to check the installed command contracts.
+The public [modeling reference](https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft/blob/69ac4646de58dc64befd804157e95120a1622803/skills/solidcraft-modeling/reference.md)
+documents these command shapes. Send each row to **SolidCraft**, in order:
+
+| Tool | Arguments |
+|---|---|
+| `execute` | `{"command":"solid.box","params":{"length":40,"width":30,"height":10,"corner":[0,0,0],"body_name":"Plate"}}` |
+| `execute` | `{"command":"solid.hole","params":{"position":[20,15,10],"diameter":6}}` |
+| `measure` | `{}` |
+| `inspect_design` | `{}` |
+| `save` | `{"path":"/home/USER/cad-cam-demo/plate.sc"}` |
+
+The box starts at its low corner, not its centre. A hole with no `depth`
+goes through all. Check for one final body, bounds from [0,0,0] to
+[40,30,10], and the hole through the top face. Inspect feature errors before
+saving. Keep the native model cache enabled when saving `.sc`.
+Do not treat a tool's success message as proof of the shape.
+
+CamCraft reads `.sc` and `.solidcraft` containers, but only their cached
+final geometry. It does not replay SolidCraft's parameters, sketches or
+feature history. The current reader requires:
+
+- one final B-rep body, not multiple bodies, a mesh body or an assembly instance;
+- document units `mm`;
+- a valid cache whose document and payload SHA-256 digests match;
+- a supported container/cache layout and `SCBREP05` body encoding.
+
+The current cache layouts are `solidcraft-model-cache/8` and
+`solidcraft-model-cache/10`, with producer `solidcraft-truck-adapter/4`.
+A newer SolidCraft save can be incompatible even when its extension is `.sc`.
+Read a refusal; do not bypass it or rename the extension.
+
+If native import is refused, use **SolidCraft** `export` with
+`{"path":"/home/USER/cad-cam-demo/plate.step","format":"step"}`.
+Then use that STEP path for the CamCraft import and link below.
+Export only the intended part when the design has other bodies; use
+SolidCraft's `bodies` export filter with the actual body names. STEP is a
+geometry hand-off, not a parametric or cross-app history transfer.
+
+### 2. Import and inspect the link in CamCraft
+
+Send these calls to **CamCraft**. Allow the exact file read in the window
+when prompted:
+
+| Tool | Arguments |
+|---|---|
+| `import_model` | `{"path":"/home/USER/cad-cam-demo/plate.sc","name":"Plate"}` |
+| `get_job` | `{}` |
+| `list_features` | `{"model":"Plate"}` |
+
+An import from a file already links the model. In `get_job`, inspect
+`models[].source`: it records `path` and `sha256`. Confirm the dimensions
+and orientation in the window. A name already used by a model updates that
+model, so do not reuse `Plate` for an unrelated part.
+
+To explicitly link an existing model, use **CamCraft** `set_model_link`
+with `{"model":"Plate","path":"/home/USER/cad-cam-demo/plate.sc"}`.
+This records the current file digest; it does **not** import the file.
+Use `import_model` to synchronize different geometry before setting a link.
+To stop watching, use `{"model":"Plate","path":null}` with the same tool.
+`set_model_link` is in the registry assembled by `tools.rs::all()`.
+`LinkWatch` is an internal window service, not an MCP tool to call.
+
+### 3. Make the drill operation in CamCraft
+
+This example starts with a blank already sized to the plate's outer box.
+It does not face the stock or mill its outside. Inspect and manually approve
+the example machine selection first. It is a software template, not a
+confirmed definition of your physical machine.
+
+| Tool | Arguments |
+|---|---|
+| `load_machine` | `{"builtin":"VMC 3-axis"}` |
+| `add_setup` | `{"name":"Top"}` |
+| `fit_stock` | `{"shape":"box","margin":0}` |
+| `set_wcs` | `{"origin":[0,0,10]}` |
+| `list_tool_catalog` | `{}` |
+| `list_operation_types` | `{"kind":"drill"}` |
+| `add_tool` | `{"catalog":"DR-0600"}` |
+| `add_operation` | `{"kind":"Drill","name":"Drill1","tool":"DR-0600","source":"Plate"}` |
+| `detect_holes` | `{"name":"Drill1"}` |
+| `get_job` | `{}` |
+
+Confirm that `DR-0600` is a 6 mm drill in the installed catalog. Check its
+reach, holder, feeds, spindle speed, hole coordinates, depths, break-through,
+stock and WCS before generation. The WCS here is the plate's top corner.
+`detect_holes` fills an existing Drill, Bore or Thread operation; its
+argument is the operation `name`, not the model. Check that it found exactly
+the intended hole. Do not continue with an empty or unexpected hole list.
+
+For a part with pockets instead, **CamCraft** `detect_pockets` with
+`{"model":"Plate"}` lists recognised pockets and slots without creating
+an operation. After inspection, call it with the returned feature `index`
+as `create`, a compatible document `tool`, and an operation `name`.
+For example, `{"model":"Plate","create":0,"tool":"EM-0400-2FL","name":"Pocket1"}`
+is valid only after that tool is added and feature 0 is confirmed.
+The through-hole plate does not require a pocket operation. Recognition
+uses geometry, not a promise that every CAD feature maps to a CAM operation.
+
+### 4. Generate, verify and save in CamCraft
+
+| Tool | Arguments |
+|---|---|
+| `generate` | `{"name":"Drill1"}` |
+| `verify` | `{}` |
+| `save_project` | `{"path":"/home/USER/cad-cam-demo/plate.camproj"}` |
+
+Read every generation note and verification finding. `verify` reports
+`ok`, `held_by`, operation findings and a program-level `gate`. A successful
+MCP exchange is not a passing verification. Stop on a refusal, stale path,
+blocking warning or failed gate. Correct the cause and verify again; do not
+remove a safety check to get a pass. Approve the project write when prompted.
+Keep the saved `.camproj` separate from the CAD file.
+
+## Change the CAD file without silently changing the program
+
+Save a deliberate geometry change in SolidCraft to the same `.sc` path.
+For the STEP fallback, export STEP again to the same linked STEP path;
+saving `.sc` alone does not change that STEP file.
+
+While CamCraft's project is open in the desktop window, `LinkWatch` checks
+linked files about once a second. It checks the digest after a size or
+modification-time change. A new SHA-256 queues a re-import under the same
+model name through `UpdateModel`. Affected operations become **Stale**;
+stock made from that model also updates. Nothing regenerates or posts
+by itself. A missing or unreadable source leaves the old model in place
+and reports the problem. Wait for the import to finish and inspect the
+model and operation state with `get_job` before proceeding.
+
+Recheck feature selections and run `detect_holes` again after a hole edit.
+For a pocket edit, inspect `detect_pockets` again and review its operation
+geometry and depths. Then explicitly generate and verify again. Headless
+CamCraft has no automatic watcher: repeat `import_model` with the same
+model name yourself. Absolute paths avoid ambiguity; window-relative links
+resolve against the saved project's folder.
+
+## Undo, approval and privacy boundaries
+
+- **Two undo stacks:** CamCraft `undo {}` changes only CamCraft's history.
+  SolidCraft `undo {}` changes only SolidCraft's history. A conversation is
+  not a distributed transaction. CamCraft's AI Chat **Undo Turn** does not
+  undo an external client's SolidCraft changes. Inspect both apps before
+  undoing; a person can have made edits between the agent's calls.
+- **Files are separate:** undoing an import does not undo a SolidCraft save.
+  The window watcher does not immediately reapply that same file digest
+  after an undo; another file change can trigger another import. Save
+  restored CAD geometry explicitly if that is the intended shared state.
+- **Manual confirmation:** keep the external client's approval controls on.
+  Require explicit confirmation for `post`, `load_machine` and
+  `edit_machine`, with exact arguments visible. CamCraft's live window gate
+  never auto-approves those calls. File and limit changes can also prompt.
+  A headless server does not supply this window approval UI; do not assume
+  it does. This walkthrough makes no `post` call. Before any later post,
+  a person must confirm the machine, control, post, workholding, tools,
+  offsets and output path. Software verification cannot certify a machine.
+- **Cloud privacy:** a local MCP connection does not make the external
+  agent local. Tool arguments and replies can send CAD parameters, names,
+  dimensions, file paths and screenshots to its model provider. Obtain
+  explicit permission for that data before using a cloud model. Otherwise
+  use a genuinely local/offline agent and model. Check that client's own
+  network, logging and retention settings. Keep CAD hand-off files on
+  local disk; do not paste their raw bytes into the conversation.
+- **No inherited privacy gate:** CamCraft's in-app `ai_offline_only`,
+  selection/screenshot switches and provider reply limits do not control
+  an external client. Do not assume it strips image blocks or enforces a
+  proposed per-server cloud policy. Disable image-returning tools in the
+  external client unless approved. Review read-only calls too: reading a
+  design can disclose it even when no file changes.
+
